_comment: Workspace-specific channel wiring for the organizer audit. Edit this file, not the script.
RULE — NEVER AUTO-MAP AN ALIAS. Every entry below is a human judgement that a named
channel really is that chapter's channel, and only a human may add one. An agent that
spots a likely match must PROPOSE it and wait for confirmation; it must not write the
entry itself, and it must not widen the matcher to guess. The audit is allowed to say
'no channel found' — that is a correct, recoverable answer. A wrong alias is not: it
reports a chapter as covered when it has no room, and nothing downstream re-checks it.
City keys are matched EXACTLY against the 'City' cell on the Chapters List — copy the
value, accents and all. Only the CHANNEL side is fuzzy-matched; a key that differs by an
accent or a space simply never fires, and a silent miss looks just like 'no channel found'.
'public' maps a chapter city to the channel that serves it as its own home, where the name
breaks the plain-slug convention. A city not listed here is matched automatically by slug
(and by the prefixes in 'public_prefixes', tried in the order listed). Map a city to null
to record that no channel exists; the matcher then stops and does not guess.
Several chapters may point at ONE channel — Madrid/Bilbao/Logroño all use #españa, and
San Francisco and Silicon Valley share #bay-area. That is coverage, not a regional
fallback: those chapters really do meet in that room, so each is counted as having a home.
The distinction from 'regional' below is whether the chapter's own people are actually
there, not whether the channel is exclusive to them.
'regional' maps a city to a channel that SERVES it without being its own — #india for
Chennai, #africa for Lagos. These are reported as 'regional only', never counted as
chapter coverage, because a member there has no local room.
'organizers' maps a city to its private organizer channel. Suffixes in
'organizer_suffixes' are matched automatically, so an entry is only REQUIRED when the name
breaks that pattern — but listing one that would have matched anyway is deliberate: it
pins the mapping against a future edit to the suffix list. null works here too, and stops
the suffix scan for that city.
An alias in ANY of the three tables that no longer resolves to a live channel ABORTS the
run — public, organizers and regional alike. A human confirmed that
mapping, so a broken one is a bug to fix, not a fallback to a slug guess — silently
downgrading the chapter to 'no channel' would generate advice to create a room it has.
